tip: yapmayacak is the negative future: the -ma marks not and -yacak marks will, so it means will not do.
Madem geleceksin means since you are coming. Madem opens a given-that reason and usually pairs with a command or plan, here erken gel.
Yapacağın iş means the work you will do. The -acağın ending makes a future verb describe the noun iş right after it, with no word like that.
gelince means when it comes or once it comes. Verb plus -ince links one event to the next, so Yaz gelince sets the time for the main verb.
parkta means at the park. The k in park is voiceless, so the locative takes -ta, not -da: parkta, never parkda.
Söylediğin means that you said. The -diğin ending turns the verb into a modifier before her şey, so Söylediğin her şey is everything you said.
Yarından itibaren means from tomorrow on. itibaren needs the ablative -dan on the time word, giving yarından from yarın.
Saat üçü çeyrek geçiyor means quarter past three. For minutes past the hour, the hour takes accusative -ü and geçiyor means is passing.
olacakmış means it will be, going by what was heard. The -mış after the future -acak adds an apparently or reportedly to the prediction.
maviye boyadı means painted it blue. With boyamak the resulting color takes the dative -e, so mavi becomes maviye.
temizlendi means it was cleaned. The -n inside makes temizlemek passive, so the shovel is acted on rather than doing the cleaning.
gelene kadar means until she comes. Verb plus -ene kadar marks until that happens, so Annem gelene kadar sets how long the studying lasts.
yağarken means while it rains. Adding -ken to the aorist yağar builds a while-doing clause running alongside the main action.
Babanın arabası means father's car. The owner takes genitive -nın and the thing owned takes -sı, so both ends of the pair are marked.
Ya otobüse bineriz ya da yürürüz means either we take the bus or we walk. The frame ya ... ya da sets up the two choices.
ödemiş olacağım means I will have paid. The -mış participle plus olacağım places the action as finished by a future point.
olacağını means that there will be, as the object of haber verdi. The -acağını ending packs a whole future clause into one word ending in accusative.
büyümeye devam ediyor means keeps growing. devam etmek needs the dative -e on the verbal noun, so büyüme becomes büyümeye.
